newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees budget surplus of 41.5 bln yuan Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: China sees budget surplus of 41.5 bln yuan Jan-May.

text.p: China registered a budget surplus of 41.532 billion yuan ($5.0039 billion) in the first five months of this year, the China Securities said on Friday.

In the period, national revenue was 309.104 billion yuan, excluding revenue from state debt, up 27.5 percent or 66.702 billion yuan from the same period last year and completing 36.8 percent of this year's budget, the newspaper said.
Central government revenue in the first five months was 160.395 billion yuan, up 35.9 percent compared with the same period last year, it said.
In the same period, national expenditure was 267.573 billion yuan, up 17.9 percent from the same period last year and completing 29.8 percent of the budget for this year, it said.
Central government expenditure in the period was 83.459 billion yuan, up 16.3 percent and completing 34.5 percent of this year's budget, it said.

However, the drain on tax revenue due to tax evasion and smuggling was still great and there was potential for a further increase in revenue, it said, quoting Li Hao, deputy director of the parliament's finance committee.
China should strengthen budgetary controls, curb excessive expenditure and use excess revenue to help to reduce its budget deficit and support under-developed areas, Li said.
China should further cut this year's budget deficit, expected to be about 56 billion yuan, he said, adding that the deficit for 1996 was 60 billion yuan.
